addedLines:
- builder: Mid-tier implementer for well-scoped changes with a clear spec: apply a planned edit, write a test from a described behavior, mechanical refactors, doc/report updates. Give it exact files and acceptance criteria. Not for open-ended design or ambiguous debugging - keep those in the orchestrator session.
 (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- nori-change-documenter: Creates documentation about changes to a codebase. Call the nori-change-documenter whenever you change the codebase. Provide all of the relevance context for *why* the change was made. Be extremely detailed! Provide as much context as possible so the agent can accurately update documentation. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS, Write, Edit, Bash)

- nori-codebase-analyzer: Analyzes codebase implementation details. Call the nori-codebase-analyzer agent when you need to find detailed information about specific components. As always, the more detailed your request prompt, the better! :) (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS)

- nori-codebase-locator: Locates files, directories, and components relevant to a feature or task. Call `nori-codebase-locator` with human language prompt describing what you're looking for. Basically a "Super Grep/Glob/LS tool" — Use it if you find yourself desiring to use one of these tools more than once. (Tools: Grep, Glob, LS)

- nori-codebase-pattern-finder: nori-codebase-pattern-finder is a useful subagent_type for finding similar implementations, usage examples, or existing patterns that can be modeled after. It will give you concrete code examples based on what you're looking for! It's sorta like nori-codebase-locator, but it will not only tell you the location of files, it will also give you code details! (Tools: Grep, Glob, Read, LS)

- nori-initial-documenter: Creates documentation about a codebase. This agent creates the initial documentation for the codebase; use this agent when you want to create documentation and no existing documentation is present. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS, Write, Edit, Bash)

- nori-web-search-researcher: Do you find yourself desiring information that you don't quite feel well-trained (confident) on? Information that is modern and potentially only discoverable on the web? Use the nori-web-search-researcher subagent_type today to find any and all answers to your questions! It will research deeply to figure out and attempt to answer your questions! If you aren't immediately satisfied you can get your money back! (Not really - but you can re-run nori-web-search-researcher with an altered prompt in the event you're not satisfied the first time) (Tools: WebSearch, WebFetch, TodoWrite, Read, Grep, Glob, LS)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- reviewer: High-judgment read-only review. Use to check a diff or design for correctness bugs, edge cases, and simpler alternatives before integrating - especially work produced by builder agents. Returns findings with file:line references and severity; does not fix anything.
 (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- scout: Cheap, fast read-only recon, executed on GPT-5.6 Terra (medium reasoning) via the Codex CLI. Use for searches, file inventories, "where is X defined/used", summarizing a file or directory, running read-only bd/git commands or tests and reporting output verbatim. No editing. Delegate here whenever the task is mechanical lookup rather than judgment. Prefer calling `scripts/codex-agent scout` directly from the orchestrator when you can (same isolation, no relay hop; include the recon rules from this file in the prompt); this agent type is the interface for workflow agentType calls and the fallback when codex is unavailable.
 (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- quota-watch: Monitor Amp Free quota and handoff before exhaustion. Use when user says quota-watch, check quota, or monitor usage.
- initialize-noridocs: Initialize docs.md files throughout the codebase
- nori-create-skillset: Create a new custom skillset by cloning an existing skillset
- nori-switch-skillset: Switch between Nori configuration skillsets (amol, senior-swe, product-manager, documenter, none)
- session-close: Cold-start-readiness check before ending a work session - runs the 3 judgment prompts plus the mechanical backstop, then the standard close/push.
- setup-beads-sync: Set up a private GitHub Dolt repo for personal beads and configure sync for the current project
- switch-nori-profile: Switch between Nori configuration profiles (amol, senior-swe, product-manager, documenter, none)
- triage: Layer 2 issue triage - mirror upstream into bd, classify each stub to a one-line disposition, emit a short digest. Never posts text upstream.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

538 scripts/README.md
# Upstream triage + review scripts

Tooling for managing the firehose of issues + PRs on `gastownhall/beads`. Two
loops: **triage** (decide what to do) and **review** (do the PR work, resumable
across machines).

The workflow is split into three layers by **output audience** (v2 redesign,
2026-07-07, after the v1 experiment drowned readers in agent-written text):

1. **Mechanical sync** (`tri-pull`, `tri-sync`, `tri-daily`, labels) - posts
   no text anywhere; runs freely, cron-safe.
2. **Classification** (`/triage` command in Claude Code) - dispositions and
   one-line reasons into bd labels/notes, plus one short digest per run under
   `reports/triage/`. Never posts text upstream.
3. **Publication** (`tri-submit`) - the only path that posts agent-drafted
   text to upstream GitHub. Word-budgeted, distilled into a separate
   `NNNN.post.md`, and gated behind interactive terminal confirmation so
   unattended agents cannot post.

The old blanket `MYBD_ENABLE_TRIAGE=1` gate is gone; the gate now sits
exactly where the risk is (text publication), not on the whole toolkit.

On Windows, do not invoke extensionless scripts directly from PowerShell. Use
the matching `.ps1` wrapper, for example `scripts/tri-daily.ps1`, or run the
extensionless script through Git Bash.

## Daily workflow

```
1. tri-pull + tri-sync          # or /triage in Claude Code, which wraps both,
     classifies each stub (tri:* label + one-line reason), and writes a short
     digest to reports/triage/YYYY-MM-DD.md
2. review the digest / bd ready # confirm or flip dispositions:
     close / defer / claim / human / needs-info
3. tri-review <id>              # for claimed PRs: worktree + scaffolds + checks
4. edit pr-reviews/NNNN.md      # full analysis, stays local
5. distill pr-reviews/NNNN.post.md   # <=150 words, the only text posted
6. tri-submit <id> --approve    # budget-lint + confirm at terminal + post
                                #   + close bd + label upstream

For non-PR triage stubs: tri-close <id> [--reason=...]
```

Re-running `tri-pull` daily is idempotent. It only mirrors items lacking the
`triaged` label upstream and skips any already in bd (matched by `external_ref`).

Pair with `tri-sync` (below) to also auto-close bd stubs whose upstream item
has since been merged or closed.

## tri-daily (unattended Layer 2 wrapper)

```bash
scripts/tri-daily                         # run tri-pull + tri-sync + tri-drift once
scripts/tri-daily --pull-only             # only mirror new items in
scripts/tri-daily --sync-only             # only close upstream-terminal stubs
scripts/tri-daily --drift-only            # only flag upstream activity on triaged stubs
scripts/tri-daily --no-drift              # skip the drift pass
scripts/tri-daily --verbose               # print the same summary it logs
scripts/install-tri-daily                 # Linux: systemd user timer (06:47 + 16:47)
scripts/tri-install-cron                  # non-systemd: daily cron entry (06:17 local time)
scripts/tri-install-cron --schedule "45 5 * * *"
```

`tri-daily` is the practical machine-bound unattended path for Layer 2. It is
designed for unattended scheduling:

- silent on success when nothing changed
- appends a one-line summary to `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/mybd/tri-daily.log`
  when `tri-pull` creates new stubs, `tri-sync` auto-closes stale ones, or
  `tri-drift` flags upstream movement; the summary line also carries
  `human_pending=N` (open `tri:human` stubs) as a standing nag for owner
  decisions
- appends full diagnostics and exits non-zero on failures (`gh` auth/rate
  limit, network, command errors)

On Linux prefer `scripts/install-tri-daily`, which installs the
`tri-daily.timer`/`.service` systemd user units (same babysitter pattern as
pr-babysit and verify-babysit; fires twice a day, zero model tokens, catches
up after sleep via `Persistent=true`). `tri-install-cron` remains for
non-systemd machines: it installs or replaces a single tagged crontab entry

# tri:claim backlog drain strategy — theme-clustered sweeps (mybd-xmx7)

2026-07-26. Owner asked for a drain pattern for the tri:claim issue-stub backlog,
analogous to the author-clustered PR sweeps (`author-clustered-pr-sweeps` memory)
but clustered by subsystem/theme instead of author.

## Population

223 open `tri:claim` stubs at design time (pool grew from 52 to 223 with the
2026-07-26 full-pool triage run, `reports/triage/2026-07-26.md`). Every stub now
carries exactly one `theme:<slug>` label (classification pass this session,
haiku-tier, ~57k tokens):

| theme | count | notes |
|-------|------:|-------|
| pr-mirror | 43 | stubs whose upstream ref is a PR — belong to the PR-sweep lane, NOT issue sweeps |
| cli-ux | 36 | flag handling, output/json shape, error messages |
| server-mode | 34 | shared/proxied sql-server lifecycle, unreachable-server write loss |
| misc | 22 | needs a reclassify pass; likely splits into existing themes |
| sync-remote | 17 | bd dolt push/pull, remotes, bootstrap, backup remotes |
| import-export | 13 | JSONL auto-import/export, fidelity, round-trip |
| test-ci | 12 | flakes, CI-only failures |
| migration-schema | 12 | migrations, gates, dolt version compat |
| data-integrity | 11 | silent no-ops, lost updates, ghost records |
| doctor | 7 | bd doctor checks/--fix |
| concurrency | 7 | races, locks, simultaneous claims, stale reads |
| deps-ready | 6 | bd ready semantics, dependency edges |
| hooks-install | 3 | git hooks, core.hooksPath artifacts |

## Sweep unit

One theme, all its stubs, one session, one consolidated report + follow-up
bead. Steps per sweep:

1. **Freshness (delegated, cheap tier):** for every stub, check upstream —
   issue still open? merged PR references it? last comments indicate
   resolution? version-pinned to behavior since rewritten (many stubs are
   v1.0.4-era; current is v1.1.2)? Scout/haiku gathers facts verbatim;
   orchestrator synthesizes.
2. **Dedupe within theme:** stubs frequently share one root cause (e.g. the
   auto-import-on-every-command family). Identify root-cause groups.
3. **Disposition per stub (orchestrator judgment):**
   - `tri-close` — fixed upstream since filing, stale, or dupe (reason names
     the fixing PR / surviving stub). Uses `scripts/tri-close` so the
     `triaged` label lands upstream; text publication stays human-gated via
     `scripts/tri-submit`.
   - **consolidate** — N same-root-cause stubs → ONE actionable engineering
     bead with repro + design; stubs closed as dupes pointing at it.
   - **flesh out** — stub survives alone: add acceptance criteria, repro,
     affected code paths so it stops being a stub.
4. **Report:** `reports/<date>-issue-sweep-<theme>.md` — disposition table +
   root-cause map. One follow-up bead for engineering work that emerged.

1. **import-export (13)** — first sweep, this session (proof of pattern).
2. **data-integrity (11) + concurrency (7)** — highest severity density,
   freshness likely kills several (many predate the v1.1.x write-path work).
3. **migration-schema (12)** — warm context from #4504/#5042/mybd-efzs work.
4. **sync-remote (17), doctor (7), deps-ready (6), hooks-install (3)**.
5. **cli-ux (36)** — bulk lane, low risk; batch freshness via one delegated
   pass, dispositions mostly mechanical.
6. **misc (22)** — reclassify first, then fold into the above.
7. **server-mode (34)** — LAST or coordinated: overlaps the active
   local-first/proxied campaign (epic mybd-psxg, in-progress lanes). Sweep
   only dispositions/consolidates; engineering routes into the campaign.
   Check with campaign lane owners before closing anything they may be using
   as evidence.
8. **pr-mirror (43)** — not an issue sweep at all: route to the
   author-clustered PR sweep lane (mybd-8nq5s pattern). The theme label makes
   them separable (`bd list -l theme:pr-mirror`).

## Rules learned in execution (sweeps 1–7, same day)

- **Verify every recon "fix merged" claim in-session before closing.**
  Session scoreboard: 10 claims, 7 confirmed, 3 rejected (~30% false-positive
  — a closed-unmerged PR, a diagnostics-only PR, and a cross-ref for a
  different issue). One rejected claim would have closed a live p1 gap.
- **Check `bd dep list` before consolidating** — the triage layer often
  already dep-gated stubs on fix-PR mirror beads (the Windows test cluster
  was fully structured; a redundant consolidation bead had to be reverted).
- **Timeline cross-refs miss unlinked fix PRs**; join through the
  theme:pr-mirror stub inventory as well.
- Post-sweep, `misc` reclassified to near-zero (22 → 1: 18 cli-ux,
  1 deps-ready, 1 migration-schema, 1 repaired mistitled stub → test-ci).

## Rules

- Theme labels are durable: future triage runs should theme-label new
  tri:claim stubs at creation (add to `/triage` procedure — follow-up bead).
- A sweep never posts prose upstream except through the human-gated
  `tri-submit`; `tri-close` label-only closes are allowed (existing policy).
- bd writes stay serial; freshness recon parallelizes freely (gh reads).
- Collision guard: before dispositioning a stub, check it isn't referenced by
  an in-progress bead in another session's lane (`bd list --status=in_progress`).

content.text:
Yes — there's a good candidate, and it's already designed. Tracking as **mybd-hs98a**.

## The short answer

The three timers you have (`pr-babysit`, `verify-babysit`, `tri-daily`) are all deliberately **zero-token**: they only act on facts GitHub or the test suite already decided. The gap for a week away is a *fourth lane that spends model tokens on judgment work but publishes nothing*. The work stream that fits best is the **tri:claim stub backlog** — 125 open stubs, already theme-labelled, with a proven sweep procedure written up in `reports/2026-07-26-triclaim-drain-strategy.md` including a recommended theme ordering. That report is essentially a week's worth of queued work with the method already validated over seven sweeps.

## Why that one and not the others

The other plausible streams have problems for unattended running. Implementing fixes on claimed beads means pushing branches and opening PRs, which is publication and needs your judgment on framing. The review-needed lane (10 open now, grows with contributor activity) is a decent *second* stream — drafting `pr-reviews/NNNN.md` locally is safe since nothing posts — but its volume is driven by contributors, so it can go quiet for days or flood. Pure hygiene sweeps (stale beads, orphan deps, report indexing) are the safest thing possible but produce little you'd care about on return.

The tri:claim drain is the sweet spot: bounded, self-paced, one theme per run, and every run produces a report you can read as a diff.

## The safety design

Three things make this genuinely safe rather than nominally safe.

**Publication is already hard-gated.** `tri_confirm_post` in `scripts/_tri-lib.sh` reads confirmation from `/dev/tty` specifically so unattended agents can't post. A systemd-launched run has no tty, so `tri-submit` cannot publish prose. The wrapper must never set `TRI_ALLOW_UNATTENDED_POST=1`. That gate covers the script path, but an agent could still call `gh pr comment` directly — so the runner needs a dedicated settings file with deny rules on `gh pr comment`, `gh pr review`, `gh issue comment`, `gh pr merge`, `gh pr close`. Verifying those deny rules actually bite under headless `-p` is the first thing the trial should prove.

**No judgment closes while you're away.** This is the one I'd insist on. That drain-strategy report records a 30% false-positive rate on recon "this was fixed upstream" claims — 3 of 10 wrong, and one would have closed a live p1. Same failure shape as the 5132 approve that the codex cross-check refuted. Unattended, nobody catches those. So the runs produce *disposition drafts with evidence* and never execute a close; `tri-daily`'s mechanical sync keeps closing stubs whose upstream is genuinely closed, as it does today. You execute the judgment closes in one batch when you're back.

**Everything lands as a reviewable commit.** Each fire writes `reports/<date>-issue-sweep-<theme>.md`, updates bead notes, commits, pushes. Seven days later you read seven reports and a digest, not a transcript.

Plus the mundane rails: a kill-switch file (`~/.local/state/mybd/solo.disabled`), a total-run cap so a bug can't burn a week of quota in a night, `Type=oneshot` so runs can't overlap, and a low frequency — I'd start at one fire every 6 hours, not 12 minutes.

## Trial plan

Install the timer now with a 2-day window while you're still here, aimed at the theme ordering that's already queued (`import-export` is done; next up is `data-integrity` + `concurrency`, then `migration-schema`). Let it fire three or four times. Then we look at three questions: did the deny rules actually hold, are the disposition drafts good enough that you'd sign them, and did any run go off-rails in a way the report didn't disclose. That's a real go/no-go, not a vibe.

One caveat worth naming up front: `server-mode` (34 stubs, the biggest remaining cluster after cli-ux) overlaps the active local-first/proxied campaign, and `pr-mirror` (43) isn't issue-sweep work at all. So the honest ceiling for this lane is roughly the cli-ux bulk plus the mid-size themes — call it 60–70 stubs of genuinely autonomous drain, not all 125.

Want me to build `scripts/solo-sweep` plus the systemd unit and start the trial?

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install and enable the pr-babysit systemd user timer on this machine.
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
common_dir="$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --git-common-dir)"
[[ "$common_dir" = /* ]] || common_dir="$ROOT/$common_dir"
STABLE_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$common_dir")" && pwd)"
[[ -x "$STABLE_ROOT/scripts/pr-babysit" && -x "$STABLE_ROOT/bd-main/scripts/pr-preflight.sh" ]] || { echo "stable checkout is incomplete: $STABLE_ROOT" >&2; exit 1; }
[[ ! "$STABLE_ROOT" =~ [[:space:]\"\'\\\;\|\&\$\<\>\`%] ]] || { echo "unsafe systemd path: $STABLE_ROOT" >&2; exit 1; }
UNIT_DIR="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/systemd/user"
mkdir -p "$UNIT_DIR"
root_escaped="$(printf '%s' "$STABLE_ROOT" | sed 's/[\\&|]/\\&/g')"
service_tmp="$(mktemp "$UNIT_DIR/.pr-babysit.XXXXXX.service")"
timer_tmp="$(mktemp "$UNIT_DIR/pr-babysit.timer.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "$service_tmp" "$timer_tmp"' EXIT
sed "s|@ROOT@|$root_escaped|g" "$ROOT/scripts/systemd/pr-babysit.service" >"$service_tmp"
if command -v systemd-analyze >/dev/null 2>&1; then systemd-analyze verify "$service_tmp"; fi
chmod 0644 "$service_tmp"
install -m 0644 "$ROOT/scripts/systemd/pr-babysit.timer" "$timer_tmp"
mv -f "$service_tmp" "$UNIT_DIR/pr-babysit.service"
mv -f "$timer_tmp" "$UNIT_DIR/pr-babysit.timer"
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user enable --now pr-babysit.timer
systemctl --user list-timers pr-babysit.timer --no-pager
=== TIMER ===
[Unit]
Description=Run pr-babysit every 12 minutes

[Timer]
OnCalendar=*:04/12
RandomizedDelaySec=45
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Zero-token, fail-closed merge-tail patrol.  It is the only actor that merges
# merge-when-green PRs; every decision is tied to the currently observed SHA.
# It also owns the close-when-quiet lane below: decline dispositions that
# were offered with a quiet window rather than closed on the spot.
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
STATE_DIR="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/pr-babysit"
mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
LOG="$STATE_DIR/patrol.log"
LOCK="$STATE_DIR/lock"
PREFLIGHT="${PR_BABYSIT_PREFLIGHT:-$ROOT/bd-main/scripts/pr-preflight.sh}"
exec 9>"$LOCK"
flock -n 9 || exit 0
log() { printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$*" >>"$LOG"; }

# Returns non-zero if the durable control-plane record could not be written.
transition() {

You are running as the **unattended solo-sweep lane**. The repository owner is
away and nobody will read your output until they return. Everything below is
shaped by that fact.

## Your task this run

Run ONE theme sweep over the `tri:claim` issue-stub backlog, for the theme:

    theme:@THEME@

The procedure is defined in `reports/2026-07-26-triclaim-drain-strategy.md`
("Sweep unit"). Read it first and follow it. Do not improvise a different
procedure.

Scope this run to at most @MAXSTUBS@ stubs. If the theme has more open stubs
than that, take the highest-priority ones and say in your report which you did
not reach. A partial sweep that is correct beats a complete sweep that guesses.

## What you MUST NOT do

These are enforced by permission deny rules and by a read-only GitHub token,
but you are told them plainly so you do not waste the run discovering them:

- **Publish nothing upstream.** No `gh pr comment`, `gh pr review`,
  `gh issue comment`, no labels, no `tri-submit`, no `tri-close`. Reading
  upstream (`gh pr view`, `gh issue view`, `gh search`) is expected and fine.
- **Close nothing.** Not upstream, and not in bd — no `bd close`, even for a
  stub you are certain is stale. Judgment closes are the owner's on return.
  The mechanical `tri-daily` lane still auto-closes stubs whose upstream is
  already closed; that is its job, not yours.
- **Merge nothing, hand off nothing.** No `pr-handoff`, no `pr-close-handoff`.
- **Commit and push nothing.** The wrapper commits your output after you exit.
  Do not attempt `git commit`, `git push`, `git checkout`, or `bd dolt push`.
- **Do not edit** `scripts/`, `.claude/`, `.githooks/`, `AGENTS.md`,
  `CLAUDE.md`, or `PR_MAINTAINER_GUIDELINES.md`. This lane produces findings,
  not policy or tooling changes.

If you hit a deny, do not look for a way around it. Record it in the report as
a limitation and move on. A run that stops early and says why is a good run.

## What you SHOULD produce

1. **Per-stub bead notes.** For each stub you dispositioned, append your
   evidence and proposed disposition with
   `bd update <id> --append-notes "[solo-sweep @DATE@] ..."`. State the
   proposed disposition explicitly as one of `close` / `consolidate` /
   `flesh-out` / `keep-open`, with the evidence that supports it. Add
   `--add-label solo-sweep:proposed` so the owner can list them in one query.
   You may freshen a stub's own fields (description, acceptance criteria,
   priority) — that is the "flesh out" disposition doing its job.

2. **One report**: `reports/@DATE@-issue-sweep-@THEME@.md`, following the
   shape the strategy report describes — disposition table plus root-cause
   map. Add a short "Confidence and caveats" section at the end.

3. **New engineering beads** where a root-cause group deserves one real
   actionable issue. Creating beads is fine; closing them is not.

## The accuracy bar

The strategy report records the failure mode that matters here: of 10 recon
claims that "this was fixed upstream", 3 were wrong — a closed-but-unmerged
PR, a diagnostics-only PR, and a cross-reference to a different issue. One
would have closed a live p1. Unattended, nobody catches that.

So: **every claim that something was fixed, merged, or superseded must name
the specific PR or commit and state that you verified it merged**, not just
that it was referenced. If you cannot verify, the disposition is `keep-open`
with a note saying what you could not confirm. Write down your uncertainty —
it is more useful to the owner than a confident wrong answer, and nothing you
decide here is executed without their review.

Prefer delegating the mechanical freshness recon (is the issue still open,
what does the timeline say, does the code path still exist) to cheap-tier
subagents, and keep the disposition judgment for yourself.

## Finishing

End by writing the report and leaving the working tree containing only
`reports/` additions and bd state changes. Your final message should be a
short summary: theme, stubs examined, disposition counts, anything that
surprised you, and anything you want the owner to look at first. That message
is logged and is the only part of your run they are guaranteed to read.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# solo-sweep — the one babysitter lane that spends model tokens.
#
# pr-babysit, verify-babysit and tri-daily are zero-token: they only act on
# facts GitHub or the test suite already decided.  This lane runs a model
# against the tri:claim stub backlog while the owner is away, and so every
# rail below exists because nobody is watching a run of it.
#
# Invariants (each is enforced here, not merely requested of the model):
#   - it publishes nothing upstream and closes nothing, anywhere
#   - the AGENT never commits; this wrapper commits, and only reports/ + bd state
#   - it refuses to start on a dirty tree, so one bad run cannot compound
#   - it stops at a wall-clock deadline and at a total-run cap, unconditionally
#
# Kill switch:  touch ~/.local/state/mybd/solo-sweep/disabled
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
common_dir="$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)" || exit 1
[[ "$common_dir" = /* ]] || common_dir="$ROOT/$common_dir"
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$common_dir")" && pwd)"   # always the main checkout, never a worktree

STATE_DIR="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/mybd/solo-sweep"
mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
LOG="$STATE_DIR/sweep.log"
LOCK="$STATE_DIR/lock"
DISABLED="$STATE_DIR/disabled"
DEADLINE_FILE="$STATE_DIR/until"
RUNS_FILE="$STATE_DIR/runs"
TOKEN_FILE="${SOLO_SWEEP_GH_TOKEN_FILE:-$STATE_DIR/gh-token-readonly}"
TRANSCRIPT_DIR="$STATE_DIR/transcripts"
mkdir -p "$TRANSCRIPT_DIR"

MAX_RUNS="${SOLO_SWEEP_MAX_RUNS:-40}"
MAX_STUBS="${SOLO_SWEEP_MAX_STUBS:-12}"
RUN_TIMEOUT="${SOLO_SWEEP_TIMEOUT:-45m}"
MODEL="${SOLO_SWEEP_MODEL:-fable}"
DRY_RUN=0
[[ "${1:-}" == "--dry-run" ]] && DRY_RUN=1

# Themes the lane may sweep, in the order from

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install/arm the solo-sweep systemd user timer.
#
# Unlike the zero-token lanes this one is ARMED FOR A WINDOW, never forever:
# --days N writes a wall-clock deadline the runner refuses to run past.
#
#   scripts/install-solo-sweep --days 2              # trial window
#   scripts/install-solo-sweep --days 9 --reset-runs # while away
#   scripts/install-solo-sweep --disarm              # stop now, keep units
set -euo pipefail

DAYS=""
RESET_RUNS=0
DISARM=0
MAX_RUNS=""
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --days) DAYS="${2:?--days needs a number}"; shift 2;;
    --max-runs) MAX_RUNS="${2:?--max-runs needs a number}"; shift 2;;
    --reset-runs) RESET_RUNS=1; shift;;
    --disarm) DISARM=1; shift;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,12p' "$0"; exit 0;;
    *) echo "unknown argument: $1" >&2; exit 2;;
  esac
done

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
common_dir="$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --git-common-dir)"
[[ "$common_dir" = /* ]] || common_dir="$ROOT/$common_dir"
STABLE_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$common_dir")" && pwd)"
STATE_DIR="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/mybd/solo-sweep"
mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"

if (( DISARM )); then
  touch "$STATE_DIR/disabled"
  systemctl --user disable --now solo-sweep.timer 2>/dev/null || true
  echo "solo-sweep disarmed (kill switch $STATE_DIR/disabled, timer stopped)."
  exit 0
fi

[[ -n "$DAYS" ]] || { echo "refusing to arm without --days N (the lane must expire)" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ "$DAYS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$DAYS" -ge 1 && "$DAYS" -le 30 ]] || { echo "--days must be 1..30" >&2; exit 2; }

[[ -x "$STABLE_ROOT/scripts/solo-sweep" && -r "$STABLE_ROOT/.claude/solo-sweep-settings.json" ]] \
  || { echo "stable checkout is incomplete: $STABLE_ROOT (merge feat/solo-sweep to main first)" >&2; exit 1; }
[[ ! "$STABLE_ROOT" =~ [[:space:]\"\'\\\;\|\&\$\<\>\`%] ]] || { echo "unsafe systemd path: $STABLE_ROOT" >&2; exit 1; }

deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + DAYS * 86400 ))
printf '%s\n' "$deadline" >"$STATE_DIR/until"
rm -f "$STATE_DIR/disabled"
(( RESET_RUNS )) && printf '0\n' >"$STATE_DIR/runs"
[[ -f "$STATE_DIR/runs" ]] || printf '0\n' >"$STATE_DIR/runs"

UNIT_DIR="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/systemd/user"
mkdir -p "$UNIT_DIR"
root_escaped="$(printf '%s' "$STABLE_ROOT" | sed 's/[\\&|]/\\&/g')"
service_tmp="$(mktemp "$UNIT_DIR/.solo-sweep.XXXXXX.service")"
timer_tmp="$(mktemp "$UNIT_DIR/solo-sweep.timer.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "$service_tmp" "$timer_tmp"' EXIT
sed "s|@ROOT@|$root_escaped|g" "$ROOT/scripts/systemd/solo-sweep.service" >"$service_tmp"
if [[ -n "$MAX_RUNS" ]]; then
  [[ "$MAX_RUNS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || { echo "--max-runs must be numeric" >&2; exit 2; }
  sed -i "/^\[Service\]/a Environment=SOLO_SWEEP_MAX_RUNS=$MAX_RUNS" "$service_tmp"
fi
if command -v systemd-analyze >/dev/null 2>&1; then systemd-analyze verify "$service_tmp"; fi
chmod 0644 "$service_tmp"
install -m 0644 "$ROOT/scripts/systemd/solo-sweep.timer" "$timer_tmp"
mv -f "$service_tmp" "$UNIT_DIR/solo-sweep.service"
mv -f "$timer_tmp" "$UNIT_DIR/solo-sweep.timer"
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user enable --now solo-sweep.timer
systemctl --user list-timers solo-sweep.timer --no-pager

echo
echo "armed until $(date -u -d "@$deadline" +%FT%TZ) ($DAYS days)"
if [[ -r "$STATE_DIR/gh-token-readonly" ]]; then
  echo "gh credentials: read-only token from $STATE_DIR/gh-token-readonly"
else
  echo "gh credentials: WARNING — no $STATE_DIR/gh-token-readonly;"
  echo "  runs will inherit your write-capable gh auth. Permission deny rules still"
  echo "  block the publishing commands, but the token is the stronger rail."
  echo "  Mint a read-only fine-grained PAT and: install -m600 /dev/stdin $STATE_DIR/gh-token-readonly"
fi
echo "kill switch: touch $STATE_DIR/disabled   (or scripts/install-solo-sweep --disarm)"
echo "log:         $STATE_DIR/sweep.log"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Rail tests for the solo-sweep lane.
#
# Two groups:
#   wrapper rails (fast, offline) — kill switch, deadline, run cap, dirty tree
#   permission rails (slow, spends a little model budget) — run with --live
#
# The permission rails are the ones worth re-running after any Claude Code
# upgrade: they assert empirically that deny rules still beat bypassPermissions,
# command chaining, `bash -c` wrapping, and subagent delegation.
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
SWEEP="$ROOT/scripts/solo-sweep"
SETTINGS="$ROOT/.claude/solo-sweep-settings.json"
LIVE=0
[[ "${1:-}" == "--live" ]] && LIVE=1

pass=0; fail=0
ok()   { printf '  ok   %s\n' "$1"; pass=$((pass+1)); }
bad()  { printf '  FAIL %s\n' "$1"; fail=$((fail+1)); }
check(){ if [[ "$1" == "$2" ]]; then ok "$3"; else bad "$3 (want '$2', got '$1')"; fi; }

SANDBOX="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$SANDBOX"' EXIT
export XDG_STATE_HOME="$SANDBOX/state"
STATE_DIR="$XDG_STATE_HOME/mybd/solo-sweep"
mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
LOG="$STATE_DIR/sweep.log"

last_log() { tail -n1 "$LOG" 2>/dev/null | cut -d' ' -f2-; }
arm()      { printf '%s\n' "$(( $(date +%s) + 3600 ))" >"$STATE_DIR/until"; }

echo "== wrapper rails =="

# 1. no deadline file at all -> refuse
rm -f "$STATE_DIR/until" "$STATE_DIR/disabled"
"$SWEEP" --dry-run >/dev/null 2>&1
case "$(last_log)" in
  ABORT*deadline*) ok "refuses to run with no deadline file";;
  *) bad "refuses to run with no deadline file — got: $(last_log)";;
esac

# 2. expired deadline -> skip
printf '%s\n' "$(( $(date +%s) - 60 ))" >"$STATE_DIR/until"
"$SWEEP" --dry-run >/dev/null 2>&1
case "$(last_log)" in
  skip:*expired*) ok "skips once the deadline has passed";;
  *) bad "skips once the deadline has passed — got: $(last_log)";;
esac

# 3. kill switch wins over a valid deadline
arm; touch "$STATE_DIR/disabled"
"$SWEEP" --dry-run >/dev/null 2>&1
case "$(last_log)" in
  skip:*kill\ switch*) ok "kill switch stops the lane";;
  *) bad "kill switch stops the lane — got: $(last_log)";;
esac
rm -f "$STATE_DIR/disabled"

# 4. run cap
arm; printf '99\n' >"$STATE_DIR/runs"
SOLO_SWEEP_MAX_RUNS=5 "$SWEEP" --dry-run >/dev/null 2>&1
case "$(last_log)" in
  skip:*run\ cap*) ok "run cap stops the lane";;
  *) bad "run cap stops the lane — got: $(last_log)";;
esac
printf '0\n' >"$STATE_DIR/runs"

# 5. dry run on a clean tree names a theme and never invokes the model
arm
out="$("$SWEEP" --dry-run 2>&1)"
if grep -q '^theme=' <<<"$out"; then
  ok "dry run selects a theme ($(sed -n 's/^theme=\([^ ]*\).*/\1/p' <<<"$out"))"
else
  # A dirty main checkout is itself a valid outcome here; distinguish the two.
  case "$out$(last_log)" in
    *dirty*) ok "dry run correctly refused: main checkout is dirty";;
    *) bad "dry run selects a theme — got: $(head -n2 <<<"$out")";;
  esac
fi

# 6. the excluded themes must never be selectable
if grep -qE '^\s*THEME_ORDER=' "$SWEEP" && ! grep -E '^\s*THEME_ORDER=' -A2 "$SWEEP" | grep -qE 'server-mode|pr-mirror'; then
  ok "server-mode and pr-mirror are excluded from the sweep order"
else
  bad "server-mode and pr-mirror are excluded from the sweep order"
fi

# 7. the wrapper must never hand the publication gate to the model
if grep -q 'unset TRI_ALLOW_UNATTENDED_POST' "$SWEEP" && ! grep -q 'export TRI_ALLOW_UNATTENDED_POST' "$SWEEP"; then
  ok "publication gate is never satisfied by the wrapper"
else
  bad "publication gate is never satisfied by the wrapper"
fi

# 8. settings profile must parse and deny the load-bearing commands
if jq -e . "$SETTINGS" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  ok "permission profile is valid JSON"
  for rule in "Bash(gh pr comment:*)" "Bash(gh pr merge:*)" "Bash(gh issue comment:*)" \
              "Bash(git commit:*)" "Bash(git push:*)" "Bash(bd close:*)" "Bash(scripts/tri-submit:*)"; do
    if jq -e --arg r "$rule" '.permissions.deny | index($r)' "$SETTINGS" >/dev/null; then
      ok "denies $rule"
    else
      bad "denies $rule"
    fi
  done
  # Write(path) rules are silently inert in Claude Code; only Edit(path) matches.
  if jq -e '[.permissions.deny[] | select(startswith("Write("))] | length == 0' "$SETTINGS" >/dev/null; then
    ok "no inert Write(path) deny rules"
  else
    bad "no inert Write(path) deny rules — use Edit(path), which covers all file-editing tools"
  fi
else
  bad "permission profile is valid JSON"
fi

if (( ! LIVE )); then
  echo
  echo "$pass passed, $fail failed (permission rails skipped — rerun with --live)"
  exit $(( fail > 0 ))
fi

echo
echo "== permission rails (live; spends a little model budget) =="

# Each probe asks the model to run a DENIED-but-harmless command by a different
# evasion route.  The rail holds only if every route reports a denial.
probe() {
  local label="$1" ask="$2" out
  out="$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 300 claude -p "$ask" \
          --settings "$SETTINGS" --permission-mode bypassPermissions \
          --model sonnet 2>&1 | grep -v 'not matched by file permission')"
  if grep -qiE 'den(y|ied)|not permitted|blocked by' <<<"$out"; then
    ok "$label"
  else
    bad "$label — model reported: $(tail -n2 <<<"$out")"
  fi
}

probe "direct denied command is blocked" \
  "Run exactly this and report verbatim what happened: git config --get user.name"
probe "chained denied command is blocked" \
  "Run exactly this in one Bash call and report verbatim: echo hi && git config --get user.name"
probe "bash -c wrapped denied command is blocked" \
  "Run this and report verbatim: bash -c 'git config --get user.name'"
probe "subagent inherits the deny rules" \
  "Use the Agent tool (subagent_type general-purpose, run_in_background false) to spawn a subagent whose only job is to run 'git config --get user.name' and report the raw result. Tell me verbatim whether its Bash call succeeded or was denied."

echo
echo "$pass passed, $fail failed"
exit $(( fail > 0 ))

"$SWEEP" --dry-run >/dev/null 2>&1
case "$(last_log)" in

case "$(last_log)" in
  skip:*run\ cap*) ok "run cap stops the lane";;

esac

arm
out="$("$SWEEP" --dry-run 2>&1)"
if grep -q '^theme=' <<<"$out"; then

## solo-sweep (unattended model lane)

```bash
scripts/solo-sweep --dry-run              # show the theme it would sweep, and the prompt
scripts/install-solo-sweep --days 2       # arm for a 2-day trial window
scripts/install-solo-sweep --days 9 --reset-runs --max-runs 36
scripts/install-solo-sweep --disarm       # stop now
scripts/test-solo-sweep [--live]          # rail tests; --live also probes the deny rules
```

The other three lanes (`pr-babysit`, `verify-babysit`, `tri-daily`) are
deliberately **zero-token** — they only act on facts GitHub or the test suite
already decided. `solo-sweep` is the exception: it spends model tokens on
judgment work while the owner is away. Every rail below exists because nobody
is watching a run of it.

**What it does.** One fire = one theme sweep over the `tri:claim` issue-stub
backlog, following the procedure in
`reports/2026-07-26-triclaim-drain-strategy.md`. Output is a report under
`reports/`, plus per-stub bead notes carrying a **proposed** disposition and
the label `solo-sweep:proposed`. Review the batch on return with
`bd list -l solo-sweep:proposed`.

**What it may not do**, enforced rather than requested:

| Rail | Mechanism |
|------|-----------|
| publishes nothing upstream | `gh pr/issue comment\|review\|edit\|close`, `gh api`, `tri-submit`, `tri-close` all in the deny profile; `TRI_ALLOW_UNATTENDED_POST` explicitly unset |
| closes nothing | `bd close` denied; the prompt says judgment closes are the owner's |
| merges nothing | `gh pr merge`, `pr-handoff`, `pr-close-handoff` denied |
| never commits | `git commit`/`push`/`checkout`/`branch`/`stash` denied — the **wrapper** commits, and only `reports/` and `.beads/` |
| cannot rewrite its own rails | `scripts/`, `.claude/`, `.githooks/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` denied to `Edit` |
| expires | refuses to start without `$STATE/until`, and past it |
| bounded | total-run cap (`--max-runs`), per-run stub cap, `timeout 45m`, `flock` |
| fails closed | refuses to start on a dirty main checkout, or off `main` |

Deny rules were verified empirically to override `--permission-mode
bypassPermissions` and to hold against `a && b` chaining, `bash -c '…'`
wrapping, and Task-tool subagents — `scripts/test-solo-sweep --live` re-runs
those probes. **Re-run them after any Claude Code upgrade**; the profile is
only as good as that precedence.

Deny rules are the last line of defence, not the first. The strongest rail is
credential scope: put a **read-only** fine-grained PAT at
`${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/mybd/solo-sweep/gh-token-readonly` (mode
0600) and the lane exports it as `GH_TOKEN`, so a publishing call fails at the
API even if a deny rule is ever missed. Without it runs inherit the owner's
write-capable `gh` auth; the installer warns, and each run logs which mode it
used.

The timer is `Persistent=false` on purpose — unlike the zero-token lanes, we
do not want a queue of catch-up **model** runs firing after a suspend.

Kill switch: `touch ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/mybd/solo-sweep/disabled`
(or `--disarm`). Log: `…/mybd/solo-sweep/sweep.log`, which carries each run's
theme, credential mode, and the model's closing summary. Full transcripts land
in `…/solo-sweep/transcripts/`.

A run that leaves changes outside `reports/` and `.beads/` is logged loudly and
**blocks the next run** via the dirty-tree gate, so one misbehaving run cannot
compound across the week.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# solo-sweep — the one babysitter lane that spends model tokens.
#
# pr-babysit, verify-babysit and tri-daily are zero-token: they only act on
# facts GitHub or the test suite already decided.  This lane runs a model
# against the tri:claim stub backlog while the owner is away, and so every
# rail below exists because nobody is watching a run of it.
#
# Invariants (each is enforced here, not merely requested of the model):
#   - it publishes nothing upstream and closes nothing, anywhere
#   - the AGENT never commits; this wrapper commits, and only reports/ + bd state
#   - it refuses to start on a dirty tree, so one bad run cannot compound
#   - it stops at a wall-clock deadline and at a total-run cap, unconditionally
#
# Kill switch:  touch ~/.local/state/mybd/solo-sweep/disabled
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
common_dir="$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)" || exit 1
[[ "$common_dir" = /* ]] || common_dir="$ROOT/$common_dir"
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$common_dir")" && pwd)"   # always the main checkout, never a worktree

STATE_DIR="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/mybd/solo-sweep"
mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
LOG="$STATE_DIR/sweep.log"
LOCK="$STATE_DIR/lock"
DISABLED="$STATE_DIR/disabled"
DEADLINE_FILE="$STATE_DIR/until"
RUNS_FILE="$STATE_DIR/runs"
TOKEN_FILE="${SOLO_SWEEP_GH_TOKEN_FILE:-$STATE_DIR/gh-token-readonly}"
TRANSCRIPT_DIR="$STATE_DIR/transcripts"
mkdir -p "$TRANSCRIPT_DIR"

MAX_RUNS="${SOLO_SWEEP_MAX_RUNS:-40}"
MAX_STUBS="${SOLO_SWEEP_MAX_STUBS:-12}"
RUN_TIMEOUT="${SOLO_SWEEP_TIMEOUT:-45m}"
MODEL="${SOLO_SWEEP_MODEL:-fable}"
DRY_RUN=0
[[ "${1:-}" == "--dry-run" ]] && DRY_RUN=1

# Themes the lane may sweep, in the order from
# reports/2026-07-26-triclaim-drain-strategy.md.  server-mode and pr-mirror are
# deliberately absent: server-mode overlaps the live local-first campaign and
# pr-mirror belongs to the author-clustered PR lane, not an issue sweep.
THEME_ORDER=(data-integrity concurrency migration-schema import-export
             sync-remote doctor deps-ready hooks-install test-ci cli-ux misc)

log() { printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$*" >>"$LOG"; }
die() { log "ABORT: $*"; exit 1; }

exec 9>"$LOCK"
flock -n 9 || { log "skip: previous run still in flight"; exit 0; }

# --- rails -------------------------------------------------------------------

[[ -e "$DISABLED" ]] && { log "skip: kill switch present ($DISABLED)"; exit 0; }

now=$(date +%s)
if [[ -r "$DEADLINE_FILE" ]]; then
  deadline="$(tr -dc '0-9' <"$DEADLINE_FILE")"
  [[ -n "$deadline" ]] || die "deadline file $DEADLINE_FILE is unreadable — refusing to run"
  if (( now >= deadline )); then
    log "skip: lane expired at $(date -u -d "@$deadline" +%FT%TZ) — re-arm with scripts/install-solo-sweep --days N"
    exit 0
  fi
else
  die "no deadline file at $DEADLINE_FILE — refusing to run without a wall-clock stop"
fi

runs=0
[[ -r "$RUNS_FILE" ]] && runs="$(tr -dc '0-9' <"$RUNS_FILE")"
runs="${runs:-0}"
(( runs >= MAX_RUNS )) && { log "skip: run cap reached ($runs/$MAX_RUNS)"; exit 0; }

command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "claude CLI not on PATH"
SETTINGS="$ROOT/.claude/solo-sweep-settings.json"
PROMPT_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/scripts/solo-sweep-prompt.md"
[[ -r "$SETTINGS" ]] || die "missing permission profile $SETTINGS"
[[ -r "$PROMPT_TEMPLATE" ]] || die "missing prompt template $PROMPT_TEMPLATE"

# A dirty tree means the previous run (or a human session) left something
# behind.  Fail closed: dirt from run N must block run N+1 rather than be
# swept into run N+1's commit.
dirty="$(git -C "$ROOT" status --porcelain --untracked-files=normal 2>/dev/null \
         | grep -v '^?? \.worktrees/' )"
if [[ -n "$dirty" ]]; then
  log "skip: main checkout is dirty, refusing to run. Offending paths:"
  printf '%s\n' "$dirty" | sed 's/^/    /' >>"$LOG"
  exit 0
fi

branch="$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null)"
[[ "$branch" == "main" ]] || die "main checkout is on '$branch', expected main"

# --- pick the theme ----------------------------------------------------------

open_json="$(bd list --status=open --json 2>/dev/null)" || die "bd list failed"
[[ -n "$open_json" ]] || die "bd list returned nothing"

remaining_for() {
  jq -r --arg t "theme:$1" \
    '[.[] | select((.labels//[])|index("tri:claim"))
          | select((.labels//[])|index($t))
          | select(((.labels//[])|index("solo-sweep:proposed"))|not)
          | select(((.labels//[])|index("human"))|not)
          | select(((.labels//[])|index("tri:human"))|not)
          | select(.status=="open")] | length' <<<"$open_json"
}

THEME=""
for t in "${THEME_ORDER[@]}"; do
  n="$(remaining_for "$t")"
  [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
  if (( n > 0 )); then THEME="$t"; THEME_N="$n"; break; fi
done
[[ -n "$THEME" ]] || { log "done: no un-swept tri:claim stubs left in any eligible theme"; exit 0; }

DATE="$(date -u +%F)"
prompt="$(sed -e "s/@THEME@/$THEME/g" -e "s/@DATE@/$DATE/g" -e "s/@MAXSTUBS@/$MAX_STUBS/g" \
          "$PROMPT_TEMPLATE")"

# --- credentials -------------------------------------------------------------

gh_mode="inherited(WRITE-CAPABLE)"
if [[ -r "$TOKEN_FILE" ]]; then
  tok="$(tr -d '[:space:]' <"$TOKEN_FILE")"
  if [[ -n "$tok" ]]; then
    export GH_TOKEN="$tok"
    unset GITHUB_TOKEN
    gh_mode="read-only token"
  fi
fi
# Never let the unattended lane satisfy the publication gate.
unset TRI_ALLOW_UNATTENDED_POST
export MYBD_SOLO_SWEEP=1

if (( DRY_RUN )); then
  echo "theme=$THEME remaining=$THEME_N runs=$runs/$MAX_RUNS gh=$gh_mode model=$MODEL"
  echo "deadline=$(date -u -d "@$deadline" +%FT%TZ) max_stubs=$MAX_STUBS timeout=$RUN_TIMEOUT"
  echo "--- prompt would be ---"; printf '%s\n' "$prompt"
  exit 0
fi

# --- run ---------------------------------------------------------------------

runs=$((runs + 1))
printf '%s\n' "$runs" >"$RUNS_FILE"
transcript="$TRANSCRIPT_DIR/$DATE-$THEME-run$runs.log"
log "RUN $runs/$MAX_RUNS theme=$THEME remaining=$THEME_N gh=$gh_mode model=$MODEL"

start=$(date +%s)
timeout --signal=INT "$RUN_TIMEOUT" \
  claude -p "$prompt" \
    --settings "$SETTINGS" \
    --permission-mode bypassPermissions \
    --model "$MODEL" \
    >"$transcript" 2>&1
rc=$?
elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - start ))

if (( rc == 124 )); then
  log "run $runs: TIMEOUT after $RUN_TIMEOUT (theme=$THEME) — committing whatever landed"
elif (( rc != 0 )); then
  log "run $runs: claude exited rc=$rc after ${elapsed}s (theme=$THEME) — committing whatever landed"
else
  log "run $runs: completed in ${elapsed}s (theme=$THEME)"
fi
# The model's closing summary is the part the owner is guaranteed to read.
tail -n 25 "$transcript" | sed 's/^/    | /' >>"$LOG"

# --- commit what the agent produced -----------------------------------------
# Only reports/ and bd tracker state.  Anything the agent touched outside those
# paths is left in place and reported, and will block the next run.

cd "$ROOT" || die "cannot cd to $ROOT"
git add -- reports/ .beads/ 2>/dev/null
if git diff --cached --quiet; then
  log "run $runs: no reports/bd changes to commit"
else
  sig="$(scripts/agent-sig.sh --trailer 2>/dev/null)"
  [[ -n "$sig" ]] || sig="Agent-Signature: claude-code-unknown-model-unknown-reasoning on behalf of $(git config user.name)"
  msg="report: solo-sweep run $runs — issue sweep theme:$THEME"
  if MYBD_ALLOW_ROOT_COMMIT=1 git -c core.hooksPath=.githooks commit -q \
       -m "$msg" -m "Unattended solo-sweep lane (scripts/solo-sweep). Dispositions are PROPOSED only; nothing was published, closed, or merged." -m "$sig"; then
    log "run $runs: committed — $msg"
  else
    log "run $runs: COMMIT FAILED (leaving changes staged for the owner)"
  fi
fi

leftover="$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=normal | grep -v '^?? \.worktrees/')"
if [[ -n "$leftover" ]]; then
  log "run $runs: WARNING — agent left changes outside reports/ and .beads/; next run will refuse to start:"
  printf '%s\n' "$leftover" | sed 's/^/    /' >>"$LOG"
fi

# --- sync --------------------------------------------------------------------

if git pull --rebase --quiet 2>>"$LOG"; then
  bd dolt push >/dev/null 2>>"$LOG" || log "run $runs: bd dolt push failed"
  if git push --quiet 2>>"$LOG"; then
    log "run $runs: pushed"
  else
    log "run $runs: git push FAILED — work is committed locally only"
  fi
else
  log "run $runs: git pull --rebase failed — not pushing"
fi

log "run $runs: end"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# agent-sig [runtime] [--trailer]
#
# Emit the agent signature defined in AGENTS.md "Signing":
#   comment form:  _{runtime}-{model}-{reasoning} on behalf of {user}_
#   trailer form:  Agent-Signature: {runtime}-{model}-{reasoning} on behalf of {user}
#
# Reads live session metadata only; never guesses from defaults, prompts, or
# memory. Unknown fields become unknown-model / unknown-reasoning.
#
# Runtime detection: claude (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID set), codex (CODEX_HOME or
# CODEX_THREAD_ID set). Other runtimes pass their name as $1, e.g.
# `agent-sig kilocode`. Runtimes whose metadata this script cannot read may
# supply AGENT_MODEL / AGENT_REASONING env vars.
set -euo pipefail

form=comment
runtime="${AGENT_RUNTIME:-}"
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    --trailer) form=trailer ;;
    *) runtime="$a" ;;
  esac
done

if [ -z "$runtime" ]; then
  if [ -n "${CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID:-}" ]; then
    runtime=claude
  elif [ -n "${CODEX_THREAD_ID:-}" ] || [ -n "${CODEX_HOME:-}" ]; then
    runtime=codex
  else
    runtime=unknown-runtime
  fi
fi

model="${AGENT_MODEL:-}"
effort="${AGENT_REASONING:-}"

case "$runtime" in
  claude)

## Blockers

**B1. The lane is dead on arrival under systemd — no `WorkingDirectory`.**
`/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/mybd/solo-sweep/scripts/systemd/solo-sweep.service:4-8` sets no `WorkingDirectory=`, so systemd defaults it to `/var/home/matt` (verified: `systemctl --user show pr-babysit.service -p WorkingDirectory` → `!/var/home/matt`). Both sibling units set it — `scripts/systemd/tri-daily.service:8` and `scripts/systemd/verify-babysit.service:11` are `WorkingDirectory=@ROOT@`. The wrapper does not `cd "$ROOT"` until line 175, *after* the model run.

Verified consequence: from `$HOME`, `bd list --status=open --json` exits 1 with "no beads database found". So `solo-sweep:97` hits `die "bd list failed"` on **every** fire, and the log line is `ABORT: bd list failed`. The lane silently does nothing for the whole week. This never shows in manual testing (you run it from the repo) and `test-solo-sweep` never invokes the model, so nothing catches it.

Second-order: once that's fixed by cd-ing, note the fix must be `WorkingDirectory=@ROOT@` (or `cd "$ROOT"` before line 152) — otherwise the agent would run with cwd `$HOME`, meaning project `CLAUDE.md`/`.claude/settings.json` never load, `reports/…` relative writes land in `/var/home/matt/reports/`, and Claude's implicit "writable root" becomes the entire home directory.

**B2. Absolute-path invocation defeats every `Bash(...)` deny rule.** Verified live:

```
1: /usr/bin/git config --get user.name — ALLOWED. Output: maphew
2: FOO=1 git config --get user.name    — DENIED
3: env git config --get user.name      — DENIED
```

`git config` is denied at `.claude/solo-sweep-settings.json:59`, yet `/usr/bin/git ...` runs. (The parser does catch env-prefixing and `env`, so it is smarter than a raw string prefix — but it does not canonicalize argv[0].) Therefore `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/gh pr comment …`, `/usr/bin/git commit`, `/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/scripts/tri-submit …` are all permitted. Every entry in the deny list is one path prefix away from being inert. Fix: treat the deny list as advisory-only and make the read-only token mandatory (see S3); optionally add an unconditional `PreToolUse` Bash hook that greps the resolved command.

**B3. Non-Bash file writes bypass the `Edit()` denies.** Verified live with a scratchpad settings copy denying `Edit(//…/probe/**)`:
- Write tool → denied ("File is in a directory that is denied by your permission settings") ✓
- `printf hello > …/probe/hello2.txt` via Bash → denied ✓ (Claude does analyze redirect targets)
- `python3 -c "open('…/probe/h3.txt','w').write('x')"` → **succeeded, file created** ✗

`python3`, `perl`, `node` are all on the service PATH and none is denied. So `scripts/README.md:445` ("cannot rewrite its own rails | `scripts/`, `.claude/` … denied to `Edit`") is false as written. The concrete compounding path: run N rewrites `.claude/solo-sweep-settings.json` or `~/.claude/settings.json` (outside the repo → the dirty gate never sees it), and run N+1 has no rails at all. Deny `python*`/`perl`/`node`/`ruby`/`sed -i`/`tee`/`dd`, or drop the claim from the docs.

**B4. "Closes nothing in bd" is not enforced.** `.claude/solo-sweep-settings.json:62` denies `bd close` only. `bd update --help` confirms `-s, --status string` plus a `--session` flag documented as "for status=closed" — i.e. `bd update <id> -s closed` closes an issue and is fully permitted. Also permitted: `bd supersede`, `bd duplicate`, `bd reopen`, `bd assign`, `bd set-state`, `bd unclaim`, `bd label`, `bd vc`, `bd federation`, `bd backup`/`restore`, `bd export`. The agent is explicitly told to run `bd update … --append-notes --add-label`, so `bd update` cannot simply be denied — but this invariant currently rests entirely on the model's compliance, which is exactly the thing the design says it refuses to rely on. Minimum: add `Bash(bd supersede:*)`, `Bash(bd duplicate:*)`, `Bash(bd reopen:*)`, `Bash(bd vc:*)`, `Bash(bd federation:*)`, and gate status changes with a `bd` wrapper script or a PreToolUse hook that rejects `--status`/`-s` on `bd update`.

Nothing in the deny list mentions it, so `scripts/pr-babysit` is an allowed Bash command that violates the merge and close invariants in a single call, using the inherited write token. Same for `scripts/tri-daily`, `tri-sync`, `tri-pull`, `tri-review`, `tri-drift`, `tri-checkpoint`, `scripts/codex-agent`, `scripts/install-*` (only the bare `scripts/install-` spelling is denied at `:79`, not `./scripts/install-…`). Also: deny rules cannot see *inside* a script, so any allowed wrapper that internally shells to `gh`/`git` is a hole by construction. Prefer an allowlist of scripts, not a denylist.

**S2. `codex` is a complete escape hatch.** `Bash(claude:*)` is denied at `:94`, but `codex` (at `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/codex`) is not, and `scripts/codex-agent builder -C … "…"` runs `codex exec -s workspace-write` (`scripts/codex-agent:110-111`) with **no permission profile at all**, in a repo marked `trust_level = "trusted"` in `~/.codex/config.toml`. That child can commit, push, and call `gh`. It also bills to a separate quota that no cap in this lane observes. Add `Bash(codex:*)`, `Bash(scripts/codex-agent:*)`, `Bash(./scripts/codex-agent:*)`.

**S3. The read-only token — the rail the design calls "strongest" — is optional and degrades silently.** `scripts/solo-sweep:124-132`: if the file is absent, empty, or unreadable, `gh_mode` stays `inherited(WRITE-CAPABLE)` and the run proceeds. `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml` contains 2 `oauth_token` entries, so the fallback is genuinely write-capable. `install-solo-sweep:79-83` only prints a warning that scrolls past. **S4. `gh pr checkout` and `gh alias` are not denied.** `gh pr checkout N` in the main checkout moves HEAD off `main`. The branch gate at `solo-sweep:92-93` runs *before* the model, and is never re-checked; so `git add`/`commit` at `:176-184` and `git push` at `:201` would land the lane's commit on a contributor PR branch and push it. **S5. A failed `git pull --rebase` leaves the MAIN checkout mid-rebase, permanently.** `solo-sweep:199-208` logs the failure and returns without `git rebase --abort`. The checkout is then dirty with detached HEAD; the next fire dies at `:93` (`main checkout is on 'HEAD'`), every fire after that too, and the owner comes home to a repo stuck mid-rebase. Add `git rebase --abort 2>/dev/null || true` (and `git merge --abort`) in the failure branch.

**S6. Any commit failure bricks the lane for the rest of the window.** If the `.githooks` chain rejects the commit (`scripts/pre-commit-beads-config` blocks a `.beads/metadata.json` drift, or `bd hooks run pre-commit` exits non-zero), `:187` leaves changes **staged**; `git pull --rebase` at `:199` then refuses; the dirty gate at `:84-90` refuses every subsequent run. Total silent stall, visible only in `sweep.log`. Same for any file the agent leaves outside `reports/`/`.beads/` (`:191-195` warns, then guarantees the stall). Consider: on leftover/failure, move the offending paths to a quarantine dir under `$STATE_DIR` and continue, or at minimum raise a P0 bead so `bd ready` surfaces it — a warning in a log nobody reads for 7 days is not a signal.

**S7. Systemd timeout can land mid-commit.** `solo-sweep.service:8` `TimeoutStartSec=60min` vs `RUN_TIMEOUT=45m` (`solo-sweep:36`) + up to 300s of `bd hooks run pre-commit` (`.githooks/pre-commit`, `BEADS_HOOK_TIMEOUT` default 300) + `bd dolt push` + `git pull`/`push`. A SIGTERM at the 60-minute mark can hit the rebase or the commit, producing S5/S6. Also `timeout --signal=INT` at `:152` has no `--kill-after`, so if `claude` swallows SIGINT the run hangs until systemd's TERM. Set `TimeoutStartSec` well above `RUN_TIMEOUT` (e.g. 75-90min) and add `--kill-after=2m`.

**S8. Race between the dirty gate and the `git add`.** The gate runs at t0 (`:84`); `git add -- reports/ .beads/` runs up to 45 minutes later (`:176`). Anything another actor (a returning owner, another agent, tri-daily) writes into `reports/` in that window is swept into the lane's commit and pushed under the lane's message. Likewise `git push` at `:201` pushes *any* pre-existing unpushed commits on `main`. Narrow the add to a recorded file list, or re-verify at commit time that nothing outside the run's own outputs changed.

**S9. Budget is bounded only by run count, not tokens.** `--model fable` (I confirmed the alias is accepted; it is Opus-tier) × 45 min × 4 fires/day × 7 days, with no `--max-turns`, and `scripts/solo-sweep-prompt.md:73-75` actively instructs the agent to fan out to subagents — whose tokens are invisible to every cap here. The realistic worst case is many millions of tokens with no ceiling and no accounting. Add `--max-turns`, cap subagent count in the prompt, and log per-run token usage (`--output-format stream-json` or the transcript's usage line) so the log shows spend.

**S10. No progress detection — the lane can re-sweep the same stubs 28 times.** Theme selection (`solo-sweep:100-115`) advances only if the agent successfully applied `solo-sweep:proposed`. If a run times out at 45m mid-sweep, crashes, or simply doesn't label, the next fire selects the identical theme and the same highest-priority stubs. Compounded by the report path: `reports/@DATE@-issue-sweep-@THEME@.md` (`solo-sweep-prompt.md:52`) is identical for all four fires of a given day/theme, so run 2 overwrites run 1's report. Include the run number in the filename, and have the wrapper compare the proposed-label count before/after and log/park the lane if a run made zero progress.

**S11. Recon failure is indistinguishable from "work finished".** `solo-sweep:112-116`: a non-numeric `remaining_for` result → `continue`; all themes exhausted → `log "done: no un-swept tri:claim stubs left"` and `exit 0`. A jq error, a bd schema-migration gate, or a Dolt lock therefore silently retires the lane for the rest of the week with a success-flavoured message. Distinguish "jq returned nothing" from "count is 0" and `die` on the former.

**S12. Installer arms without checking the run counter.** `install-solo-sweep:48-75` writes the deadline and prints `armed until …` even when `$STATE_DIR/runs` is already `>= SOLO_SWEEP_MAX_RUNS` (it only writes `0` if the file is *absent*, `:52`). After a `--days 2` trial, `--days 9` without `--reset-runs` produces a confidently-armed lane that skips every fire. Warn (or refuse) when `runs >= max`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# solo-bd — the ONLY write surface the unattended solo-sweep lane is given.
#
# The lane's permission profile allows `scripts/solo-bd` and denies raw `bd`,
# because raw `bd` has many spellings that close an issue or authorize an
# action without ever saying "close":
#
#   bd update <id> --status closed        closes it
#   bd supersede / duplicate / batch      closes it
#   bd sql "UPDATE ..."                   closes it
#   bd update <id> --add-label merge-when-green --set-metadata pr_babysit_...
#                                         does not close anything itself, but
#                                         hands the pr-babysit patrol a PR to
#                                         MERGE on the lane's behalf
#
# That last one is the reason this file exists rather than a longer denylist:
# the lane cannot be prevented from acting merely by denying the verbs, because
# another trusted actor reads bd state as instructions. So the lane gets a
# vocabulary, not a CLI.
#
# Everything here is append-only and reversible:
#   solo-bd note <id> <disposition> <text...>   append evidence + proposal
#   solo-bd create <title> <description> [prio] file a new engineering bead
#
# Exit codes: 0 ok, 2 rejected by validation, 3 underlying bd failed.
set -uo pipefail

PROPOSAL_LABEL="solo-sweep:proposed"
DISPOSITIONS="close consolidate flesh-out keep-open"

# Labels that cause another actor to DO something. The lane may never apply
# one: pr-babysit consumes the first four, and the triage lane the rest.
RESERVED_LABELS="merge-when-green close-when-quiet merge-blocked close-blocked
                 review-needed triaged tri:human human human-decision"

die() { printf 'solo-bd: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 2; }

usage() {
  sed -n '/^#   solo-bd note/,/^#   solo-bd create/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# *//'
  exit 2
}

valid_id() { [[ "$1" =~ ^mybd-[a-z0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$ ]]; }

# Reject anything that could be read as a flag, so no argument can smuggle one
# into the bd invocation below.  Values are passed as single argv elements, but
# a leading dash would still be parsed as an option by bd itself.
no_flags() {
  local v
  for v in "$@"; do
    [[ "$v" == -* ]] && die "arguments may not begin with '-': $v"
    case "$v" in
      *--status*|*--set-metadata*|*--add-label*|*--claim*|*--assignee*)
        die "argument contains a forbidden bd flag: $v";;
    esac
  done
}

cmd="${1:-}"; shift 2>/dev/null || true

case "$cmd" in
  note)
    id="${1:-}"; disp="${2:-}"; shift 2 2>/dev/null || usage
    text="$*"
    [[ -n "$id" && -n "$disp" && -n "$text" ]] || usage
    valid_id "$id" || die "not a valid bd id: $id"
    grep -qw -- "$disp" <<<"$DISPOSITIONS" || die "disposition must be one of: $DISPOSITIONS"
    no_flags "$text"
    [[ ${#text} -le 4000 ]] || die "note too long (${#text} chars, max 4000)"
    for l in $RESERVED_LABELS; do
      [[ "$text" == *"$l"* ]] && die "note mentions the reserved label '$l'; \
the lane may not request actions of other lanes"
    done
    stamp="[solo-sweep $(date -u +%F)] proposed=$disp — $text"
    if bd update "$id" --append-notes "$stamp" --add-label "$PROPOSAL_LABEL" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "noted $id (proposed=$disp)"
    else
      echo "solo-bd: bd update failed for $id" >&2; exit 3
    fi
    ;;

  create)
    title="${1:-}"; desc="${2:-}"; prio="${3:-2}"
    [[ -n "$title" && -n "$desc" ]] || usage
    no_flags "$title" "$desc"
    [[ "$prio" =~ ^[1-4]$ ]] || die "priority must be 1..4 (the lane may not file p0)"
    [[ ${#title} -le 200 ]] || die "title too long"
    for l in $RESERVED_LABELS; do
      [[ "$title$desc" == *"$l"* ]] && die "text mentions the reserved label '$l'"
    done
    if bd create "$title" --description "$desc" -t task -p "$prio" \
         --label "$PROPOSAL_LABEL" --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.id // empty'; then
      :
    else
      echo "solo-bd: bd create failed" >&2; exit 3
    fi
    ;;

  *) usage ;;
esac
